FUNK ROCK [funk] — Los Angeles 1984. The Red Hot Chili Peppers, "The
Red Hot Chili Peppers" (Bijou Studios, Los Angeles; EMI America,
August 1984). PAUL NAMED THE BAND AND THE MAP CHOSE THE RECORD: Blood
Sugar Sex Magik is 1991 and `powerballad` holds Los Angeles 1991, so
the row takes the band's own debut instead — cut in Los Angeles, in a
free year, and seven years EARLIER, which is what lets `numetal` above
declare it as an ancestor at all.
MEASURED over 15 files (Red Hot Chili Peppers 10 · Rage Against the
Machine 7 · Faith No More 1 — the corpus's whole funk-metal holding,
and the RHCP files are Californication-era rather than the debut,
which the row states rather than hiding). Tempo (n=15): p10 75 · p25
84 · med 95 · p75 123. Mode 10 minor / 5 major. THE FIELD THAT NAMES
IT is the bass histogram, and nothing else in this round looks like
it: 9384646393748484 — an onset on FOURTEEN of sixteen steps, against
grunge's 9151717171717171 and poppunk's 9061807080718080, which are
eighths. That is the slap, and `bassStyle: "sixteenths"` is that
number. Off-16 fraction 0.30, the highest of the rock rows; hat plain
eighths; snare 2120923533219136, ghosted everywhere.
  kick  9143513171624131   snare 2120923533219136

LINEAGE: `funk` (Cincinnati 1967) is the sixteenth-note hand and
the one-chord vamp, and it takes the largest share; `punk` (New
York 1976) is the speed and the shouting; `hardcore` (Washington
1980) is the Californian half of that; `psychfunk` (Detroit 1975)
is the fuzz guitar over the groove, which is the actual sound.

THE SLAP BASS IS A CHAIR, not a bass line: on this music the bass
plays the tune and the guitar answers, which is the inversion the
genre exists to make. The generated bass underneath keeps the
sixteenths measured above.

THE MODE THIS RECORD CANNOT SOUND (2026-09-02, the catalogue round,
shift 2; test/precompose.test.js G14b).
Red Hot Chili Peppers, Los Angeles 1984 — this row's own act and year. The
roots above are bVII-i-i-III: degrees 6, 0 and 2. Degree 6 IS used, which is
why this row looks different from the others in the sweep — but the degree
DORIAN exists for is 5, the natural sixth, and it is never reached, so mixo
and dorian and aeolian all map {6,0,2} to the same three pitch classes.
MEASURED: dorian -> aeolian moved not one rendered note. A flat-seven root
over a minor third is a natural-minor cell and the field now says so. A vi
chord was NOT bolted on to rescue the word: funk rock does not play one, and
inventing a root to justify a label is the failure this check exists to
catch, not a way to pass it.

CLOSEST, ANSWERED 2026-09-03 (the catalogue round, shift 3). The QA report's
`closest` column ranks each declared parent against every older row by a FEATURE
VECTOR — bpm, swing, major/minor, kit density, harmony kind, plan, nobass,
instrumental, family — and calls a parent sitting in the further half of that
ranking suspect. The vector has no term for the thing a child actually TAKES
from a parent, so an ancestor the record deliberately departs from ranks far by
construction, and the catalogue's trunk rows — funk, jazz, swing, ballad,
ambient, punk, drone, gregorian — rank far from nearly every leaf they grew.
THE PARENTS ON THIS ROW STAND. What the vector cannot see: `funk` and `psychfunk` are the BASS AND THE DRUMS — the sixteenth-note slap and
the one, which is what this music is — and the vector reads a rock tempo and a
rock kit as distance from both. `acidrock` (1967) is offered as nearer; Hendrix's
guitar is genuinely in this lineage, and it arrives through `psychfunk`, which is
already declared, rather than as a second edge to the same fact.

THE DRUMS WERE UNDER THE WAH (2026-09-03). Paul, listening: "Funk rock drums
are super low." And then, having found it before the probe did: "the reason
the funk drums are low is the auto-wah is on them." He is right, and the row
was not at fault: `fx: ["wah"]` below is the RECORD-WIDE character chip, and
since the 2026-08-27 dealing round a chip goes onto every chair "INCLUDING THE
BASS AND THE DRUMS" (precompose.js deskThe) — so this record's kick and hat
were being played through a resonant bandpass parked at 320 Hz at a mix of 0.9.
MEASURED at the ring (the mute-complement press, upstream of the master rider)
at seed 1 over 8 bars, with the chip off the DRUM units only: drums solo
-31.01 -> -25.45 dB, the kit's contribution to the record 1.44 -> 3.82 dB, the
kick -40.24 -> -28.42, the hat -48.84 -> -37.44, and the band without drums
unchanged at -27.20. That 3.82 sits against `funk`'s 3.74 and `punk`'s 2.68 at
the same seed — this row's own parents, neither of which carries a chip.
THE FIX IS A LAW AND NOT A NUMBER ON THIS ROW: audio/desk.js `kitless` refuses
a filter-type chip (wah, fenv, filtersweep) on a drum unit, for the 19 rows
that name one. Paul had asked for the kit +30% before the cause was found; the
cause was worth 5.56 dB, so no lift was added on top of it, and the wah still
plays on every pitched chair the row wanted it on.
label: Los Angeles 1984
words: the bass, slapped, every sixteenth it can reach
the guitar, answering on the off-beats
